question.problem:
Maya runs a lemonade stand. The table below gives the selling rate $r(t)$ (in liters per hour) over a $6$-hour period starting at noon.

| $t\,(\text{hours})$ | $0$ | $2$ | $4$ | $6$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $r(t)\,(\text{L/hour})$ | $1$ | $k$ | $5$ | $3$ |

If the left Riemann sum approximation of the total number of liters sold over the $6$-hour period (with three subintervals defined by the given points) is $28$ liters, then what is the value of $k?$ 

$\,\,k=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The area $A$ under the curve $y=r(t)$ can be approximated using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈(\overset{\text{heights}}{\overset{⏞}{r({t}_{0})+r({t}_{1})+…+r({t}_{n-1})}})\cdot \,\,{{Δt}_{⏟}}_{\text{ }\text{width}} \\  & =(r(0)+r(2)+r(4))\cdot Δt.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we now set up a table with the values of $r(t)$ at each point:

| $t$ | $0$ | $2$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $r(t)$ | $1$ | $k$ | $5$ |

So, we obtain the following approximation to the area:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈(1+k+5)\cdot 2 \\  & =(k+6)\cdot 2 \\  & =2k+12\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, in the given context, the area under the curve represents the total number of liters sold by Maya. Since we are given that the left Riemann sum approximation of the total number of liters sold is $28,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2k+12 & =28 \\ 2k & =16 \\ k & =8.\end{aligned}
$$
